name: Core Image (CILanczosScaleTransform)
baseline: UIGraphicsImageRenderer drawing a UIImage(contentsOfFile:) into a smaller context
verdict_reason: NSHipster measured 2.4983 s against 0.1420 s for UIKit (about 17.6x slower) with a shared GPU CIContext on an iPhone 7, and the article points to Apple's own Core Image performance guidance to crop and downsample with Core Graphics or Image I/O instead. Forcing the software renderer was an order of magnitude slower again.
tier_reason: Independent measurement (NSHipster) with public code and the device and OS stated, run in the Debug test configuration.
claimed_speedup: No speedup measured: Core Image 2.4983 s vs UIKit 0.1420 s (17.6x slower, derived from page data); the software renderer was 'an order of magnitude slower' still.
workload: Load a 12,000 px square, 20 MB JPEG from disk, scale it to 100 x 100 with CILanczosScaleTransform through a shared GPU CIContext and return a UIImage; average of XCTest measure() iterations.
toolchain: Swift 5.0; Debug test configuration in the example project's scheme
one_liner: Core Image's Lanczos scale filter; resizing a JPEG from disk was about 17.6x slower than UIGraphicsImageRenderer on an iPhone 7.
how_it_is_fast: Core Image builds a filter graph and renders it on the GPU through a CIContext, applying a Lanczos kernel. For a one-off resize that means decoding the full image, uploading it, rendering and reading back, which outweighs the GPU's arithmetic advantage.
use_it_when: Resizing is one step in a longer Core Image filter chain that stays on the GPU, such as photo or video effects
You need Lanczos quality and already render through a shared CIContext
skip_it_when: One-off resizing of images loaded from disk or the network
Creating a CIContext per call, or using the software renderer
caveats: Debug test configuration; the timed work is mostly inside Apple's frameworks
iPhone 7 with iOS 12.2 (2019); Core Image's Metal backend has changed since
Decode, render and readback are timed together
tradeoffs: Needs a long-lived CIContext and GPU access

evidence.quote: performed on an iPhone 7 running iOS 12.2,
yielded results an order of magnitude slower than base results.
you should use Core Graphics or Image I/O functions to crop and downsample images instead of Core Image.
